workflow.title: From Baobab to a Mac: investigate a large folder before removing it
workflow.intent: Help GNOME/Baobab users moving to macOS preserve a deliberate inspect-before-delete workflow, including the option to retain Baobab via Homebrew.
workflow.description: Baobab's folder-size workflow can carry over to a Mac. Start with the folder and its contents, not a deletion target; choose between the documented Homebrew package and a broader Mac maintenance preview without treating chart sizes as recoverable space.
outline: Place official Baobab scan image directly after the lead, credited and undated.
Separate folder size, accessible scan coverage and available disk space; cite permissions caveat without repeating old implementation details.
Choose one folder, inspect its children and identify whether files are personal originals, reproducible outputs or unknown app data. These are editorial decision steps, not reported testing.
Retain Baobab through Homebrew if its documented analysis workflow is the job; disclose package targets/dependencies and untested Mac behavior.
Explain GNOME's documented selected-folder Trash action, backup and restore/rebuild consequences; never recommend emptying Trash automatically.
Use the labelled Breathing Room Space preview later to distinguish category/app/project views and broader source-level monitoring, with affiliation, preview, Python and hosted-AI caveats.
End with a decision checklist rather than a repeated sales pitch.
workflow.interactionPass: Handoff a no-upload, non-executing checklist: Is the folder understood? Is it an original? Is there a backup or verified rebuild path? If unknown, stop. It must not classify actual files or promise safe deletion.
